title: What to know about the Green Line shutdowns planned for August
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: MBTA Green Line service suspended on multiple branches in August for tunnel upgrades and accessibility improvements.
Free shuttle buses replace service with connections to the Orange Line; expect 25-minute additional travel time.
Symphony Station closed until 2029; additional temporary station closures and changes on C and E branches planned.

title: Suffolk corrections officer killed after stopping to help stranded motorist in Boxford
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Brett Martin, a 51-year-old Suffolk corrections officer, was fatally struck on I-95 in Boxford while helping a stranded driver.
Massachusetts State Police responded to the incident at 8:30 p.m. Monday, and Martin was later pronounced dead at a hospital.
The Essex County District Attorney’s Office is investigating; Martin joined the Suffolk Sheriff's Department in February 2008.

title: Review & setlist: Tame Impala reimagines the bounds of arena rock at TD Garden
author: Perry Eaton
bullets: Tame Impala performed at TD Garden, showcasing a new 360-degree stage setup for an immersive concert experience.
Opening act Djo, featuring Stranger Things' Joe Keery, performed energetic retro rockers from the album 'The Crux'.
Tame Impala's set included tracks from 'The Slow Rush' and 'Lonerism', with special lighting and visual effects enhancing the show.

title: Electric utility rates are going up Aug. 1. Will your bill actually increase?
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Massachusetts electric rates will rise on Aug. 1, affecting customers of National Grid, Eversource, and Unitil.
Eversource's basic service rate increases from 15.6 to 17.3 cents per kilowatt-hour due to supply costs.
Most Massachusetts residents are unaffected as only 26.6% use basic service; others use municipal or competitive suppliers.

title: Man called in bomb threat after getting kicked out of Boston movie theater, police say
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 55-year-old man, Christopher McFadden, was arrested for making a bomb threat at Boston's AMC theater.
McFadden was removed from the theater for harassing an employee and later allegedly called in the threat.
Police traced the bomb threat call to McFadden's phone, arrested him at a restaurant, and held him at Nashua Street Jail.

title: In new ‘milestone,’ Rhode Island nonprofit tags first hammerhead shark
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Atlantic Shark Institute tagged its first hammerhead shark near Block Island, marking a milestone for the Rhode Island nonprofit.
Climate change is leading hammerhead sharks, typically found in warmer waters, to venture further north, nearing New England waters.
The tagged hammerhead shark will be tracked using satellite and acoustic tags, aiding research on shark migration and habitat use.

title: Panera is moving its headquarters to this Boston suburb
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Panera will move its headquarters to Weston, Massachusetts, aiming to open by July 2027 as part of its 'Panera Rise' strategy.
The company will keep a support center in St. Louis but transfer many employees and remote positions to the new Weston headquarters.
CEO Paul Carbone, a Boston-area native, previously worked with Dunkin’ Brands, SharkNinja, and Talbots before joining Panera Brands.

title: How new MBTA pilot programs aim to save riders money
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Gov. Maura Healey announced MBTA pilot programs to make public transportation more affordable, starting in September 2026.
A pilot program will offer nearly unlimited transfers within two hours, reducing complexity and cost for riders.
Free fares will be available for seniors 75 and older without a driver's license, across all MBTA services.

title: Two Concord residents die in head-on crash
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Two Concord residents, John and Paula Hamilton, died after a head-on crash on Walden Street Saturday.
The crash involved a Honda Accord crossing into oncoming traffic, colliding with the Hamiltons' Tesla Model 3.
Three others, including two passengers from Tacoma and the Honda driver, were injured and hospitalized.

title: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with ex-husband expected back on the stand
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Patrick Clancy is expected to testify again in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial, describing her as 'normal' before the murders.
Lindsay Clancy, accused of killing her children, is using an insanity defense citing postpartum mental illness and intrusive thoughts.
Prosecutors argue Lindsay Clancy acted intentionally, rejecting the claim she was suffering from postpartum psychosis at the time.
